correct_completion: to buy bread on the way home.
full_sentence: He stopped to buy bread on the way home.

options.text: buy bread on the way home.
options.why_wrong: A bare infinitive cannot follow 'stopped' in this position, so the sentence is ungrammatical.

options.text: buying bread on the way home.
options.why_wrong: 'Stop' followed by a gerund means to quit an activity, so this says he ended a habit of buying bread, not that he paused to do it.

options.text: to buy bread on the way home.
bought bread on the way home.
options.why_wrong: A past tense verb cannot follow 'stopped' directly, so this form breaks the grammar of the sentence.

grammar_focus: Verbs followed by gerund versus to-infinitive: stop + to-infinitive for purpose
explanation: 'Stop' followed by a gerund means to quit an activity, while 'stop' followed by a to-infinitive means to pause in order to do something else. Learners may confuse the two because their first language expresses purpose with a full clause rather than an infinitive.
translation: Zatrzymał się, żeby kupić chleb w drodze do domu.
